/docs/api/types.ts

types.ts

Metadata types for library source code analysis.

These types represent the structure of src/lib/ exports, extracted at build time via TypeScript compiler analysis. Used for generating API documentation and enabling code search.

Hierarchy: ModuleJson → DeclarationJson (discriminated union on kind) → MemberJson (discriminated union on kind)

Input/output split

The schemas are fuz_schema schemas. Array fields default to [] and boolean flags to false (s.with_default_fn, s.with_default), so they're optional in serialized JSON (compact) but guaranteed after parsing. Input types (ModuleJsonInput, DeclarationJsonInput, ComponentPropJsonInput) accept the omitted fields; output types (ModuleJson, DeclarationJson, ComponentPropJson) guarantee them. Use compactReplacer (in declaration-helpers.ts) with JSON.stringify for compact output, and parseModuleJson (or parseAnalyzeResult in analyze-core.ts) to validate and restore the defaults — the parse helpers are the stable entry points, independent of the schema library.

Array defaults are factories (s.with_default_fn(…, () => [])): s.with_default returns its value as-is, so a literal [] would be one array shared by every parse.

Discriminated union

DeclarationJson is an s.variant on kind over these variants: FunctionDeclarationJson, ClassDeclarationJson, InterfaceDeclarationJson, TypeDeclarationJson, VariableDeclarationJson, EnumDeclarationJson, ComponentDeclarationJson, SnippetDeclarationJson, NamespaceDeclarationJson. Each variant has only the fields relevant to that kind, enforced by s.object. Use isKind (in declaration-helpers.ts) to narrow.

MemberJson is similarly an s.variant on kind, over FunctionMemberJson, VariableMemberJson, ConstructorMemberJson. Each variant has only the fields relevant to that member kind.

Internal analysis code that constructs declarations incrementally uses DeclarationJsonBuild — a permissive interface with all fields optional. Validation at the parseModuleJson boundary enforces variant correctness.

see also

  • declaration-helpers.ts for display formatting and type narrowing utilities

  • analyze.ts for the main analysis entry points

  • tsdoc.ts for JSDoc/TSDoc extraction into these types

  • postprocess.ts for post-processing (mergeReExports, findDuplicates)

A class declaration. Has members, extends, implements.

import {ClassDeclarationJson} from 'svelte-docinfo/types.ts';

inheritance

extends: SchemaStrictObjectOutput<typeof ClassDeclarationJsonEntries>

members

kind
: "class"
#
extends
: string[]
#

Extended base class — 0 or 1 entries (TypeScript allows only one base). An array so every heritage field (extends, implements, externalTypes, InterfaceDeclarationJson.extends) shares one shape; consumers iterate heritage uniformly instead of branching on kind.

Verbatim text of this declaration's own heritage clause (as is implements), so it is spelled as this module wrote it and resolves in its scope — a local rename stays the local name, where externalTypes resolves renames because its walk crosses modules.

see also

  • implements (this variant), InterfaceDeclarationJson.extends for the other verbatim heritage fields, externalTypes (this variant) for the resolved external reach.

extendsInfo
: TypeJson[]
#

Structured form of each extends entry, index-aligned with it: always one node per entry, so the usual absence contract (see TypeJson) is relaxed here and a bare Base is a reference node. It follows the written entry as GenericParamJson.constraintInfo does, and a locally renamed import carries its exported name, where the text beside it keeps the local one; a base that isn't a class or interface by name (extends mixin(B), a const holding a class) is a terminal node over its text.

externalTypes
: string[]
#

External types the extends chain reaches whose contributions members never enumerates — the class counterpart of InterfaceDeclarationJson.externalTypes, descending through local base classes. implements contributes nothing: an implemented interface adds no members, the class declares its own.

Entry normalization (rename resolution, type-parameter substitution, text-dedupe, source order) matches TypeDeclarationJson.externalTypes. A direct external base makes this textually equal to extends; consumers dedupe at render time.

implements
: string[]
#

Implemented interfaces.

implementsInfo
: TypeJson[]
#

Structured form of each implements entry, index-aligned with it, as extendsInfo is.

members
: (FunctionMemberJson | VariableMemberJson | ConstructorMemberJson)[]
#

Class members: methods, properties, constructors, getters/setters — own members only, inherited members excluded whatever their origin. Source order, except accessors (getter/setter pairs merged by name), which follow every other member.

alsoExportedFrom
: string[]
#

Module paths (relative to sourceRoot) that re-export this declaration under the same name. The canonical declaration lives in this module's declarations array; these paths are additional import locations for the same thing.

The same edges appear from the re-exporting side as ModuleJson.reExports — use that when asking "what does this module re-export" instead of inverting these arrays. The two can disagree at the margins: a reExports entry whose canonical declaration is @nodocs (or whose module isn't in the analyzed set) has no back-link here.

Consumer note: To build a complete re-export map, scan two fields:

  1. alsoExportedFrom on each declaration — same-name re-exports
  2. aliasOf on declarations — renamed re-exports (separate declarations)
partial
: boolean
#

Whether extraction failed partway through, leaving some fields missing (e.g., typeSignature, parameters).

examples
: string[]
#

Code examples from @example tags.

seeAlso
: string[]
#

Related items from @see tags, in raw TSDoc format.

throws
: ThrowsJson[]
#

Exceptions from @throws tags. type is the tag's written type, and typeInfo its structured form, present for a braced type (@throws {A<B>}) that isn't the whole story as text (see TypeJson); an unbraced tag's leading word never has one, nor does a tag in a component's HTML @component comment, which is read as text.

name
: string
#

The exported name. Always populated. The default-export slot is named 'default', except a Svelte component, which takes its filename-derived name ('X' for X.svelte) — 'default' is the symbol's actual name in JS (import {default as X} and ns.default both expose it directly), and import X from 'mod' is sugar for import {default as X}. Consumers branch on name === 'default' to render the sugar form when desired.

modifiers
: ("public" | "protected" | "readonly" | "static" | "abstract" | "getter" | "setter")[]
#

TypeScript modifiers like readonly, static, or protected.

genericParams
: GenericParamJson[]
#

Generic type parameters like <T, U>.

aliasOf
?: { module: string; name: string; }
#

For renamed re-exports (export {foo as bar}), points to the original declaration. This declaration's name is the alias; aliasOf.name is the original name.

For renames out of the default slot (export {default as bar} from './x' where ./x is export default ...), aliasOf.name is 'default' — the canonical's actual symbol name. Consumers locate the canonical by (aliasOf.module, aliasOf.name).

Svelte component exception: when the source is a .svelte file (e.g., export {default as Foo} from './X.svelte'), the canonical's name is the component name (derived from the filename), so aliasOf.name is the component name ('X'), NOT 'default'. Consumers that branch on aliasOf.name === 'default' to detect default-rename should additionally check whether aliasOf.module ends with .svelte.

Different from alsoExportedFrom: aliases create new API surface names, while alsoExportedFrom tracks additional import paths for the same name.

A type-only rename of a value (export type {someConst as c} from './x') synthesizes a normal alias — declarations carry no type-only marker.

deprecatedMessage
?: string
#

Deprecation message from @deprecated tag.

since
?: string
#

Version introduced, from @since tag.

internalMessage
?: string
#

Internal-API marker from the @internal tag. Presence means the tag was written; an empty string is a bare tag with no trailing prose.

A marker, not an exclusion: @internal means "not stable public API" (TSDoc semantics) while the declaration, member, or prop stays documented — unlike @nodocs, which removes a declaration from output entirely (and is ignored on props and members).

mutates
?: Record<string, string>
#

Mutation documentation from @mutates tags (non-standard), mapping keys to descriptions.

Keys are intentionally unvalidated — typically a parameter name, but authors may also use compound paths (this.foo, obj.field) or multi-word external state references. Backticks are stripped from keys so `` a `` and a normalize to one key; an empty-string value is a bare tag with no description. The schema accepts any string key so consumers can render whatever the author wrote.

On a component prop it declares the component's mutation contract for the value it's handed: the component writes into the prop's object or array in place (@mutates items - appends the selected entry, @mutates options.cache - fills on first render). Reassigning a prop is not a mutation in this sense (bindable covers it), though a $bindable prop can carry both.

docComment
?: string
#

JSDoc/TSDoc comment.

typeSignature
?: string
#

Full TypeScript type signature.

sourceLine
?: number
#

1-based line in the source file, a positive integer. Synthesized aliases (see aliasOf) carry the local export specifier's line, not the canonical's.

ComponentCssPropertyJson
#

types.ts view source

value + type

also exported from index.ts

A CSS custom property in a Svelte component's styling API: one a consumer sets on the component (<A --a_color="red" />) or on an ancestor, read by the component's styles.

Maps onto a Custom Elements Manifest cssProperties entry field for field (name, description, syntax, default); fallback, sourceLine, and documented have no CEM counterpart.

import {ComponentCssPropertyJson} from 'svelte-docinfo/types.ts';

inheritance

extends: SchemaStrictObjectOutput<typeof ComponentCssPropertyJsonEntries>

members

name
: string
#

The custom property's name as written, -- included (--a_color); case-sensitive, as in CSS.

sourceLine
: number
#

1-based line in the original .svelte source of the property's first var() read, or for a documented property the component never reads, of its @cssprop tag.

documented
: boolean
#

Whether a @cssprop tag in the component's doc comment documents the property, as opposed to the fallback-read heuristic (or an @property rule) finding it alone. A consumer can list only the documented entries when a component has any, dropping the global tokens the heuristic also catches.

description
?: string
#

The @cssprop tag's description, raw like docComment. Only on a documented entry.

syntax
?: string
#

The property's value syntax, verbatim, unvalidated: the @cssprop tag's braced syntax (@cssprop {<color>} --a gives <color>), else the syntax descriptor of an @property rule for the name in the component's style, its quotes stripped (syntax: '<color>' gives <color>).

fallback
?: string
#

What the style gives the property when a consumer doesn't set it: the initial-value of an @property rule for the name in the component's style (a registered property is never unset, so its initial value applies whatever a read falls back to), else the fallback of the first var() read with one, the verbatim source text after the comma, trimmed, comments included (var(--a, var(--b, 1px)) gives var(--b, 1px)). Empty for var(--a,), a fallback of nothing. Absent for a documented property no read gives a fallback. Code fact only; the tag's claim is default, and cssprop_default_mismatch warns when the two disagree.

default
?: string
#

The @cssprop tag's bracketed default (@cssprop [--a=1px] gives 1px), verbatim and trimmed. Only on a documented entry. The author's claim beside fallback, the style's fact; a renderer wanting one value takes default ?? fallback.

see also

  • ComponentDeclarationJson.cssCustomProperties for which reads count

ComponentDeclarationJson
#

types.ts view source

value + type

also exported from index.ts

A Svelte component declaration. Has props, externalTypes, acceptsChildren, cssCustomProperties.

import {ComponentDeclarationJson} from 'svelte-docinfo/types.ts';

inheritance

extends: SchemaStrictObjectOutput<typeof ComponentDeclarationJsonEntries>

members

kind
: "component"
#
externalTypes
: string[]
#

External types whose properties are filtered out of props — the attribute bags a component forwards, such as HTMLButtonAttributes or SvelteHTMLElements['button']. A bag stays listed when some of its properties are documented anyway because the $props() destructuring names them (see props).

Covers every way props compose them: an intersection or union branch, a bare or indexed-access annotation, and interface Props extends Bag (directly or through a local base). Entries carry the written form with the same normalizations as TypeDeclarationJson.externalTypes: import renames at the definition site resolve to the exported name, and a type parameter bound inside the descent substitutes its written argument — interface A<T> extends HTMLAttributes<T> reached via `Props extends A<HTMLDivElement> records HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`. The component's *own* generics stay in scope and emit as written (HTMLAttributes<T> beside the genericParams documenting T). Each distinct bag appears once, in source order; a local name is used only when it hides a definition the walk cannot traverse (a mapped or conditional type). Names carry no module, so two distinct bags sharing an exported name collapse to one entry.

see also

  • TypeDeclarationJson.externalTypes for the full entry contract, InterfaceDeclarationJson.externalTypes for the field on the props interface itself. Field shapes mirror TS syntax.

props
: ComponentPropJson[]
#

Svelte component props, in source order.

Properties an external type contributes are left out (externalTypes names their bags), except the ones the $props() destructuring names: type in let {type = 'button', ...rest}: HTMLButtonAttributes = $props() is documented with the external declaration's type and JSDoc. Renamed (class: className) and nested (a: {b}) elements name their prop; the rest element names nothing, and a name the props type has only through an index signature isn't admitted. Admitted props follow the others, in destructuring order, since their declaration position is in a package.

acceptsChildren
: boolean
#

Whether the component accepts children: an explicit or inherited Snippet-typed children prop, implicit template usage, or a default slot (<slot /> or a declared $$Slots) in a legacy component, one svelte2tsx reads as runes-less. A runes component's <slot /> doesn't set it, and neither does a named slot alone.

cssCustomProperties
: ComponentCssPropertyJson[]
#

The component's styling API: the CSS custom properties its styles read with a fallback (var(--a, 1px)), the pattern Svelte's own docs give for a component's styling hooks, or read bare and register with @property, and leave for a consumer to set, plus the ones its doc comment documents with @cssprop. One entry per name: the documented ones first, in tag order, then the rest in the order of each name's first read.

A read counts when it's an outermost var(), not one in another var()'s fallback: var(--a, var(--b)) reads --a, with --b the fallback chain's global token. Reads anywhere in the top-level <style> count, in :global(…) rules, nested rules, @media/@container/@supports blocks, and keyframes alike, and so do reads in the static text of the markup's style attributes and style: directives on elements and style and --a attributes on child components (<Child --a="var(--b, 1px)" /> reads --b). A name drops out when the component sets it itself: a --a: … declaration in its <style>, a style:--a directive, or a --a: in a style attribute on one of its elements. A --a or style attribute on a child component sets nothing, since it styles the child. A name read only without a fallback isn't listed, unless the style registers it with @property --a {…}, whose syntax and initial-value the entry carries (the last rule for a name wins; inherits isn't modeled); a registered name nothing reads isn't listed either: bare reads are mostly global design tokens. A global token read with a fallback is listed too; the author's fix is to drop the fallback or to document the property with @cssprop. There's deliberately no option to filter names at analysis: the output keeps every read, and a consumer that wants less filters it (to documented entries, say). Names are case-sensitive, as in CSS.

@cssprop --a - Description 1 (or @cssproperty) in the component's doc comment, the source that wins docComment (the in-script JSDoc over the HTML @component comment, the losing one's tags ignored), lists --a whatever the heuristic makes of it, documented: true, with the tag's description, syntax, and default. It merges with the read: a bare read, one nested in another's fallback, one the component sets itself, or one in its markup's static style text counts, giving sourceLine and fallback. A name the component never reads stays, at the tag's line, and warns unknown_cssprop; a tag default the style's fallback disagrees with warns cssprop_default_mismatch; a tag that names no property warns malformed_tag, and one repeating a name duplicate_tag, each dropped.

Without tags, empty when the component has no <style> and no markup read, when its style's lang (or type) names a preprocessor language (css_lang_unsupported), or when Svelte's parser rejects the component (css_parse_failed); tagged properties are listed even then.

alsoExportedFrom
: string[]
#

Module paths (relative to sourceRoot) that re-export this declaration under the same name. The canonical declaration lives in this module's declarations array; these paths are additional import locations for the same thing.

Keys are intentionally unvalidated — typically a parameter name, but authors may also use compound paths (this.foo, obj.field) or multi-word external state references. Backticks are stripped from keys so `` a `` and a normalize to one key; an empty-string value is a bare tag with no description. The schema accepts any string key so consumers can render whatever the author wrote.

On a component prop it declares the component's mutation contract for the value it's handed: the component writes into the prop's object or array in place (@mutates items - appends the selected entry, @mutates options.cache - fills on first render). Reassigning a prop is not a mutation in this sense (bindable covers it), though a $bindable prop can carry both.

docComment
?: string
#

JSDoc/TSDoc comment.

typeSignature
?: string
#

Full TypeScript type signature.

sourceLine
?: number
#

1-based line in the source file, a positive integer. Synthesized aliases (see aliasOf) carry the local export specifier's line, not the canonical's.

ComponentDeclarationJsonInput
#

types.ts view source

The input ComponentDeclarationJson parses, with any field it defaults optional.

import type {ComponentDeclarationJsonInput} from 'svelte-docinfo/types.ts';

inheritance

extends: SchemaStrictObjectInput<typeof ComponentDeclarationJsonEntries>

members

kind
: "component"
#
name
: string
#

The exported name. Always populated. The default-export slot is named 'default', except a Svelte component, which takes its filename-derived name ('X' for X.svelte) — 'default' is the symbol's actual name in JS (import {default as X} and ns.default both expose it directly), and import X from 'mod' is sugar for import {default as X}. Consumers branch on name === 'default' to render the sugar form when desired.

externalTypes
?: string[]
#

External types whose properties are filtered out of props — the attribute bags a component forwards, such as HTMLButtonAttributes or SvelteHTMLElements['button']. A bag stays listed when some of its properties are documented anyway because the $props() destructuring names them (see props).

Covers every way props compose them: an intersection or union branch, a bare or indexed-access annotation, and interface Props extends Bag (directly or through a local base). Entries carry the written form with the same normalizations as TypeDeclarationJson.externalTypes: import renames at the definition site resolve to the exported name, and a type parameter bound inside the descent substitutes its written argument — interface A<T> extends HTMLAttributes<T> reached via `Props extends A<HTMLDivElement> records HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`. The component's *own* generics stay in scope and emit as written (HTMLAttributes<T> beside the genericParams documenting T). Each distinct bag appears once, in source order; a local name is used only when it hides a definition the walk cannot traverse (a mapped or conditional type). Names carry no module, so two distinct bags sharing an exported name collapse to one entry.

see also

  • TypeDeclarationJson.externalTypes for the full entry contract, InterfaceDeclarationJson.externalTypes for the field on the props interface itself. Field shapes mirror TS syntax.

props
?: ComponentPropJsonInput[]
#

Svelte component props, in source order.

Properties an external type contributes are left out (externalTypes names their bags), except the ones the $props() destructuring names: type in let {type = 'button', ...rest}: HTMLButtonAttributes = $props() is documented with the external declaration's type and JSDoc. Renamed (class: className) and nested (a: {b}) elements name their prop; the rest element names nothing, and a name the props type has only through an index signature isn't admitted. Admitted props follow the others, in destructuring order, since their declaration position is in a package.

acceptsChildren
?: boolean
#

Whether the component accepts children: an explicit or inherited Snippet-typed children prop, implicit template usage, or a default slot (<slot /> or a declared $$Slots) in a legacy component, one svelte2tsx reads as runes-less. A runes component's <slot /> doesn't set it, and neither does a named slot alone.

cssCustomProperties
?: ComponentCssPropertyJsonInput[]
#

The component's styling API: the CSS custom properties its styles read with a fallback (var(--a, 1px)), the pattern Svelte's own docs give for a component's styling hooks, or read bare and register with @property, and leave for a consumer to set, plus the ones its doc comment documents with @cssprop. One entry per name: the documented ones first, in tag order, then the rest in the order of each name's first read.

A read counts when it's an outermost var(), not one in another var()'s fallback: var(--a, var(--b)) reads --a, with --b the fallback chain's global token. Reads anywhere in the top-level <style> count, in :global(…) rules, nested rules, @media/@container/@supports blocks, and keyframes alike, and so do reads in the static text of the markup's style attributes and style: directives on elements and style and --a attributes on child components (<Child --a="var(--b, 1px)" /> reads --b). A name drops out when the component sets it itself: a --a: … declaration in its <style>, a style:--a directive, or a --a: in a style attribute on one of its elements. A --a or style attribute on a child component sets nothing, since it styles the child. A name read only without a fallback isn't listed, unless the style registers it with @property --a {…}, whose syntax and initial-value the entry carries (the last rule for a name wins; inherits isn't modeled); a registered name nothing reads isn't listed either: bare reads are mostly global design tokens. A global token read with a fallback is listed too; the author's fix is to drop the fallback or to document the property with @cssprop. There's deliberately no option to filter names at analysis: the output keeps every read, and a consumer that wants less filters it (to documented entries, say). Names are case-sensitive, as in CSS.

@cssprop --a - Description 1 (or @cssproperty) in the component's doc comment, the source that wins docComment (the in-script JSDoc over the HTML @component comment, the losing one's tags ignored), lists --a whatever the heuristic makes of it, documented: true, with the tag's description, syntax, and default. It merges with the read: a bare read, one nested in another's fallback, one the component sets itself, or one in its markup's static style text counts, giving sourceLine and fallback. A name the component never reads stays, at the tag's line, and warns unknown_cssprop; a tag default the style's fallback disagrees with warns cssprop_default_mismatch; a tag that names no property warns malformed_tag, and one repeating a name duplicate_tag, each dropped.

Without tags, empty when the component has no <style> and no markup read, when its style's lang (or type) names a preprocessor language (css_lang_unsupported), or when Svelte's parser rejects the component (css_parse_failed); tagged properties are listed even then.

lang
?: "js"
#

Script language. undefined means TypeScript (default), 'js' for JS-only components.

alsoExportedFrom
?: string[]
#

Module paths (relative to sourceRoot) that re-export this declaration under the same name. The canonical declaration lives in this module's declarations array; these paths are additional import locations for the same thing.

The same edges appear from the re-exporting side as ModuleJson.reExports — use that when asking "what does this module re-export" instead of inverting these arrays. The two can disagree at the margins: a reExports entry whose canonical declaration is @nodocs (or whose module isn't in the analyzed set) has no back-link here.

Consumer note: To build a complete re-export map, scan two fields:

  1. alsoExportedFrom on each declaration — same-name re-exports
  2. aliasOf on declarations — renamed re-exports (separate declarations)
aliasOf
?: { module: string; name: string; }
#

For renamed re-exports (export {foo as bar}), points to the original declaration. This declaration's name is the alias; aliasOf.name is the original name.

For renames out of the default slot (export {default as bar} from './x' where ./x is export default ...), aliasOf.name is 'default' — the canonical's actual symbol name. Consumers locate the canonical by (aliasOf.module, aliasOf.name).

Svelte component exception: when the source is a .svelte file (e.g., export {default as Foo} from './X.svelte'), the canonical's name is the component name (derived from the filename), so aliasOf.name is the component name ('X'), NOT 'default'. Consumers that branch on aliasOf.name === 'default' to detect default-rename should additionally check whether aliasOf.module ends with .svelte.

Different from alsoExportedFrom: aliases create new API surface names, while alsoExportedFrom tracks additional import paths for the same name.

A type-only rename of a value (export type {someConst as c} from './x') synthesizes a normal alias — declarations carry no type-only marker.

partial
?: boolean
#

Whether extraction failed partway through, leaving some fields missing (e.g., typeSignature, parameters).

examples
?: string[]
#

Code examples from @example tags.

deprecatedMessage
?: string
#

Deprecation message from @deprecated tag.

seeAlso
?: string[]
#

Related items from @see tags, in raw TSDoc format.

throws
?: ThrowsJsonInput[]
#

Exceptions from @throws tags. type is the tag's written type, and typeInfo its structured form, present for a braced type (@throws {A<B>}) that isn't the whole story as text (see TypeJson); an unbraced tag's leading word never has one, nor does a tag in a component's HTML @component comment, which is read as text.

ComponentPropJson
#

types.ts view source

value + type

also exported from index.ts

Component prop information for Svelte components.

Standalone schema (not extending ParameterJson) because component props have different semantics: named attributes with no positional order (<Foo {a} {b} /> = <Foo {b} {a} />), no rest parameters, and support for two-way binding (the $bindable rune, or a legacy export let prop).

?: TypeJson

?: TypeJson

?: string

defaultValue
?: string
#

The destructuring default's source text, else the @default tag text — verbatim author text either way ("'primary'", () => 10), quotes included, no normalization; consumers render it as highlighted TS.

parameters
?: ParameterJson[]
#

Structured parameters for callable props: a snippet's (Snippet<[text: string]>) or a callback's ((value: string) => void). returnType tells the two apart — a callback has one, a snippet doesn't.

Present when the prop has extractable parameters, absent otherwise. Only populated when there are actual parameters — bare Snippet / Snippet<[]> and a zero-parameter callback do not set this field. Intentionally optional without a default, unlike the other array fields (see the input/output split in the module comment): absence is a meaningful signal, not an empty list.

returnType
?: string
#

A callback prop's return type, and the marker that the prop is one: present exactly when the prop's type has a call signature this project declared (onpick?: (value: string) => void, or a project alias for one). parameters holds that signature's parameters.

The prop's type is read with null and the optional undefined stripped, so (() => void) | null is a callback. A union of several function types is not — typeInfo lists its members instead.

Only project-declared signatures count, as for callable members. A prop typed wholly by a package (MouseEventHandler<HTMLButtonElement>, a Component) carries neither field, since an external callable isn't always a callback. In an intersection of an own signature with an external one (MouseEventHandler<HTMLElement> & (() => void), the shape a redeclared onclick over an attributes bag takes), the own signature is the one described. Of several own signatures, the first.

returnTypeInfo
?: TypeJson
#

Structured return type; absent when returnType is the whole story (see TypeJson).

ConstructorMemberJson
#

types.ts view source

value + type

also exported from index.ts

A constructor member (class constructor, construct signature). Has parameters, overloads — but not returnType/returnDescription (constructors always return their class).

name is narrowed to two literal sentinels: 'constructor' for class constructors and '(construct)' for interface/type-alias construct signatures (which share kind: 'constructor' but originate from getConstructSignatures() on a non-class type — no user-chosen identifier exists). The literal is preserved (rather than omitted) so getDisplayName and consumer renderers reading member.name keep working without a constructor-specific branch.

type "public" | "protected" | "readonly" | "static" | "abstract" | "getter" | "setter"

TypeScript modifier keywords extracted from declarations.

Only modifiers that appear on public API members are included. Private members (including #field syntax) are filtered out during analysis. Protected members are included as part of the extension API.

Enum members: name/value pairs with optional JSDoc.

alsoExportedFrom
: string[]
#

Module paths (relative to sourceRoot) that re-export this declaration under the same name. The canonical declaration lives in this module's declarations array; these paths are additional import locations for the same thing.

The same edges appear from the re-exporting side as ModuleJson.reExports — use that when asking "what does this module re-export" instead of inverting these arrays. The two can disagree at the margins: a reExports entry whose canonical declaration is @nodocs (or whose module isn't in the analyzed set) has no back-link here.

Consumer note: To build a complete re-export map, scan two fields:

  1. alsoExportedFrom on each declaration — same-name re-exports
  2. aliasOf on declarations — renamed re-exports (separate declarations)

: boolean

Code examples from @example tags.

seeAlso
: string[]
#

Related items from @see tags, in raw TSDoc format.

throws
: ThrowsJson[]
#

Exceptions from @throws tags. type is the tag's written type, and typeInfo its structured form, present for a braced type (@throws {A<B>}) that isn't the whole story as text (see TypeJson); an unbraced tag's leading word never has one, nor does a tag in a component's HTML @component comment, which is read as text.

name
: string
#

The exported name. Always populated. The default-export slot is named 'default', except a Svelte component, which takes its filename-derived name ('X' for X.svelte) — 'default' is the symbol's actual name in JS (import {default as X} and ns.default both expose it directly), and import X from 'mod' is sugar for import {default as X}. Consumers branch on name === 'default' to render the sugar form when desired.

modifiers
: ("public" | "protected" | "readonly" | "static" | "abstract" | "getter" | "setter")[]
#

TypeScript modifiers like readonly, static, or protected.

genericParams
: GenericParamJson[]
#

Generic type parameters like <T, U>.

aliasOf
?: { module: string; name: string; }
#

For renamed re-exports (export {foo as bar}), points to the original declaration. This declaration's name is the alias; aliasOf.name is the original name.

For renames out of the default slot (export {default as bar} from './x' where ./x is export default ...), aliasOf.name is 'default' — the canonical's actual symbol name. Consumers locate the canonical by (aliasOf.module, aliasOf.name).

Svelte component exception: when the source is a .svelte file (e.g., export {default as Foo} from './X.svelte'), the canonical's name is the component name (derived from the filename), so aliasOf.name is the component name ('X'), NOT 'default'. Consumers that branch on aliasOf.name === 'default' to detect default-rename should additionally check whether aliasOf.module ends with .svelte.

Different from alsoExportedFrom: aliases create new API surface names, while alsoExportedFrom tracks additional import paths for the same name.

A type-only rename of a value (export type {someConst as c} from './x') synthesizes a normal alias — declarations carry no type-only marker.

deprecatedMessage
?: string
#

Deprecation message from @deprecated tag.

since
?: string
#

Version introduced, from @since tag.

internalMessage
?: string
#

Internal-API marker from the @internal tag. Presence means the tag was written; an empty string is a bare tag with no trailing prose.

A marker, not an exclusion: @internal means "not stable public API" (TSDoc semantics) while the declaration, member, or prop stays documented — unlike @nodocs, which removes a declaration from output entirely (and is ignored on props and members).

mutates
?: Record<string, string>
#

Mutation documentation from @mutates tags (non-standard), mapping keys to descriptions.

Keys are intentionally unvalidated — typically a parameter name, but authors may also use compound paths (this.foo, obj.field) or multi-word external state references. Backticks are stripped from keys so `` a `` and a normalize to one key; an empty-string value is a bare tag with no description. The schema accepts any string key so consumers can render whatever the author wrote.

On a component prop it declares the component's mutation contract for the value it's handed: the component writes into the prop's object or array in place (@mutates items - appends the selected entry, @mutates options.cache - fills on first render). Reassigning a prop is not a mutation in this sense (bindable covers it), though a $bindable prop can carry both.

docComment
?: string
#

JSDoc/TSDoc comment.

typeSignature
?: string
#

Full TypeScript type signature.

sourceLine
?: number
#

1-based line in the source file, a positive integer. Synthesized aliases (see aliasOf) carry the local export specifier's line, not the canonical's.

ExternalReExportJson
#

types.ts view source

value + type

also exported from index.ts

A re-export whose immediate target is an external package — export {x} from 'pkg', export {x as y} from 'pkg', or export * as ns from 'pkg'. External is per createIsExternalPath; a project-local target excluded from output (the internal/ convention) is not external, and its re-exports synthesize alias declarations instead.

specifier is the module specifier as written (usually a package name); there is no canonical declaration to resolve, so these entries are flat facts about the statement rather than edges into the module graph.

Only statements that *directly* reference the external specifier are captured. Forms that stay silent: import {x} from 'pkg'; export {x}; (import-then-export), re-export chains that reach a package through another source module (that module owns the entry) or through a project-local gated module, and specifiers the checker can't resolve. Statement-level @nodocs suppresses the entry.

optional

property
: boolean
#

Whether the member is a function-typed property (now: () => number) and not a method (now(): number), on an interface or a type alias. The two classify alike, as callables, so a renderer reads this to write the property form, the only one that takes readonly or a default. Set unless one of the property's declarations uses method syntax, so a property with no declaration (a mapped type's) is one too. Never set on a class member: a class's methods are methods, and a field holding a function is a variable.

Mutation documentation from @mutates tags (non-standard), mapping keys to descriptions.

Keys are intentionally unvalidated — typically a parameter name, but authors may also use compound paths (this.foo, obj.field) or multi-word external state references. Reassigning a prop is not a mutation in this sense (bindable covers it), though a $bindable prop can carry both.

Whether the member is a function-typed property (now: () => number) and not a method (now(): number), on an interface or a type alias. The two classify alike, as callables, so a renderer reads this to write the property form, the only one that takes readonly or a default. An interface declaration. Has members, extends.

import {InterfaceDeclarationJson} from 'svelte-docinfo/types.ts';

inheritance

extends: SchemaStrictObjectOutput<typeof InterfaceDeclarationJsonEntries>

members

kind
: "interface"
#
extends
: string[]
#

Extended interfaces.

Verbatim text of this declaration's own heritage clause, so entries are spelled as this module wrote them and resolve in its scope — a local rename (import type {Bag as B}) stays B. Unlike externalTypes, whose walk crosses modules and therefore resolves renames back to the exported name, this clause never leaves the declaring file.

see also

  • ClassDeclarationJson.extends, ClassDeclarationJson.implements for the other verbatim heritage fields, externalTypes (this variant) for the resolved external reach.

extendsInfo
: TypeJson[]
#

Structured form of each extends entry, index-aligned with it: always one node per entry, so the usual absence contract (see TypeJson) is relaxed here and a bare Base is a reference node. It follows the written entry as GenericParamJson.constraintInfo does, and a locally renamed import carries its exported name, where the text beside it keeps the local one; a base that isn't a class or interface by name (extends mixin(B), a const holding a class) is a terminal node over its text.

externalTypes
: string[]
#

External types the heritage composition reaches whose contributions members never enumerates.

A named base's members aren't listed, and a computed heritage entry's external properties are filtered out (see members). This field names the external types behind that absence: `interface Props extends HTMLButtonAttributes records the bag directly, and interface Props extends LocalBase (where LocalBase` reaches a bag) records it transitively — the same answer the component annotated with this interface gets, where extends alone dead-ends at a possibly-unexported local name. Inherited *local* content is the extends field's business: the base is documented at its own declaration.

Entry normalization (rename resolution, type-parameter substitution, text-dedupe, source order) matches TypeDeclarationJson.externalTypes. Direct-heritage cases make this textually equal to extends; consumers dedupe at render time.

members
: (FunctionMemberJson | VariableMemberJson | ConstructorMemberJson)[]
#

Interface members: property signatures, method signatures, index signatures, call/construct signatures — the interface's own, plus what each extends entry that isn't a named interface or class contributes.

A named base (extends Base, extends Base<string>, an alias of either), local or external, keeps its members, call/construct signatures included: extends names it, and it is documented at its own declaration. A computed entry has no declaration of its own — a mapped, conditional, or utility-type instantiation (z.infer<typeof S>, Omit<Base, 'a'>, Partial<Base>), an intersection, an object type behind an alias — so it contributes what the same type documents as a type alias's members, external-origin contributions dropped and labeled in externalTypes. A name the interface declares itself wins; otherwise the first heritage entry with the name supplies it, as in TypeScript's inheritance. A call or construct signature likewise goes to the first entry that reaches it: extends Base, Base & {…} leaves Base's to Base, extends Base & {…}, Base lists them. Own members come in source order, then the contributed properties entry by entry, then their index signatures, with call/construct signatures last (own before contributed, as overloads of one member, each signature once).

A merged interface documents the block selectDeclarationNode picks, the first in declaration order: its members and its extends (own call and construct signatures excepted, which come from every block). Another block's members and heritage document nothing, and a name another block declares still drops from the documented block's heritage contribution, since TypeScript takes it from that block.

mergedValue
: boolean
#

The exported name also carries a value meaning — a merged value+type symbol (const Foo = ... + interface Foo {...}), where the interface wins the declaration slot and the value's own type goes undocumented. Tells consumers the name is importable as a runtime value: `import {Foo}, never import type {Foo} (see generateImport`).

see also

  • TypeDeclarationJson.mergedValue

alsoExportedFrom
: string[]
#

Module paths (relative to sourceRoot) that re-export this declaration under the same name. The canonical declaration lives in this module's declarations array; these paths are additional import locations for the same thing.

The same edges appear from the re-exporting side as ModuleJson.reExports — use that when asking "what does this module re-export" instead of inverting these arrays. The two can disagree at the margins: a reExports entry whose canonical declaration is @nodocs (or whose module isn't in the analyzed set) has no back-link here.

Consumer note: To build a complete re-export map, scan two fields:

  1. alsoExportedFrom on each declaration — same-name re-exports
  2. aliasOf on declarations — renamed re-exports (separate declarations)
partial
: boolean
#

Whether extraction failed partway through, leaving some fields missing (e.g., typeSignature, parameters).

examples
: string[]
#

Code examples from @example tags.

seeAlso
: string[]
#

Related items from @see tags, in raw TSDoc format.

throws
: ThrowsJson[]
#

Exceptions from @throws tags. type is the tag's written type, and typeInfo its structured form, present for a braced type (@throws {A<B>}) that isn't the whole story as text (see TypeJson); an unbraced tag's leading word never has one, nor does a tag in a component's HTML @component comment, which is read as text.

name
: string
#

The exported name. Always populated. The default-export slot is named 'default', except a Svelte component, which takes its filename-derived name ('X' for X.svelte) — 'default' is the symbol's actual name in JS (import {default as X} and ns.default both expose it directly), and import X from 'mod' is sugar for import {default as X}. Consumers branch on name === 'default' to render the sugar form when desired.

modifiers
: ("public" | "protected" | "readonly" | "static" | "abstract" | "getter" | "setter")[]
#

TypeScript modifiers like readonly, static, or protected.

genericParams
: GenericParamJson[]

Generic type parameters like <T, U>.

aliasOf
?: { module: string; name: string; }
#

For renamed re-exports (export {foo as bar}), points to the original declaration. This declaration's name is the alias; aliasOf.name is the original name.

MemberJson
#

types.ts view source

value + type

also exported from index.ts

type FunctionMemberJson | VariableMemberJson | ConstructorMemberJson

Metadata for a nested declaration within a class, interface, type, or enum.

Discriminated union on kind with 3 variants: FunctionMemberJson, VariableMemberJson, ConstructorMemberJson. Use isKind (in declaration-helpers.ts) to narrow, or check member.kind directly.

Does not include fields that exist on declarations but not on members (extends, externalTypes, implements, props, alsoExportedFrom, aliasOf).

Nesting is exactly one level deep — members never contain their own members.

value + type

also exported from index.ts

"function" | "variable" | "constructor"

type "function" | "variable" | "constructor"

The subset of declaration kinds that appear as nested members in classes, interfaces, and types.

Class members include constructors ('constructor'), methods ('function'), and properties/accessors ('variable'). Interface/type properties use the same kinds for property signatures, method signatures, index signatures, and call/construct signatures.

Every other DeclarationKind is top-level only; nesting is exactly one level deep.

ModuleJson
#

types.ts view source

value + type

also exported from index.ts

Metadata for a source module — the top-level container in the data model.

analyze, analyzeFromFiles, and AnalysisSession.query return AnalyzeResultJson, whose modules is sorted by path (compareStrings). Each module contains its exported declarations, dependency graph, and optional moduleComment.

import {ModuleJson} from 'svelte-docinfo/types.ts';

inheritance

extends: SchemaStrictObjectOutput<typeof ModuleJsonEntries>

members

dependencies
: string[]
#

Modules this imports (paths relative to sourceRoot).

dependents
: string[]
#

Modules that import this (paths relative to sourceRoot).

starExports
: string[]
#

Modules fully re-exported via export * from './module'. Paths are relative to sourceRoot. Statement-level @nodocs suppresses the entry, like the other re-export encodings. `export type * from` is recorded like a value star — per-statement type-only-ness isn't captured — and each target appears once, however many statements name it.

Only modules that are themselves in the result appear. A star over a project module that emits nothing (gated, or outside the analyzed inputs) has no entry: the bindings it projects are documented in this module as the named re-exports the star stands for — declarations with aliasOf, or reExports entries for bindings whose canonical does emit — following ES star semantics (default doesn't project, a local export shadows, a name two stars disagree on is excluded). A binding such a module re-exports from a package is not recorded anywhere.

A star over a component that failed to transform names its partial placeholder module, whose bindings are unknown (resolveExportSurface reports it unresolved); one that emits nothing (gated, never supplied) is dropped.

extends: SchemaStrictObjectOutput<typeof NamespaceDeclarationJsonEntries>

members

kind
: "namespace"
#
module
: string

Source module path (relative to sourceRoot) projected under this binding.

alsoExportedFrom
: string[]
#

Module paths (relative to sourceRoot) that re-export this declaration under the same name. The canonical declaration lives in this module's declarations array; these paths are additional import locations for the same thing.

The same edges appear from the re-exporting side as ModuleJson.reExports — use that when asking "what does this module re-export" instead of inverting these arrays. The two can disagree at the margins: a reExports entry whose canonical declaration is @nodocs (or whose module isn't in the analyzed set) has no back-link here.

Consumer note: To build a complete re-export map, scan two fields:

  1. alsoExportedFrom on each declaration — same-name re-exports
  2. aliasOf on declarations — renamed re-exports (separate declarations)
partial
: boolean
#

Whether extraction failed partway through, leaving some fields missing (e.g., typeSignature, parameters).

examples
: string[]

Code examples from @example tags.

seeAlso
: string[]

Related items from @see tags, in raw TSDoc format.

throws
: ThrowsJson[]
#

Exceptions from @throws tags. type is the tag's written type, and typeInfo its structured form, present for a braced type (@throws {A<B>}) that isn't the whole story as text (see TypeJson); an unbraced tag's leading word never has one, nor does a tag in a component's HTML @component comment, which is read as text.

name
: string
#

The exported name. Always populated. The default-export slot is named 'default', except a Svelte component, which takes its filename-derived name ('X' for X.svelte) — 'default' is the symbol's actual name in JS (import {default as X} and ns.default both expose it directly), and import X from 'mod' is sugar for import {default as X}. Consumers branch on name === 'default' to render the sugar form when desired.

modifiers
: ("public" | "protected" | "readonly" | "static" | "abstract" | "getter" | "setter")[]
#

TypeScript modifiers like readonly, static, or protected.

genericParams
: GenericParamJson[]
#

Generic type parameters like <T, U>.

aliasOf
?: { module: string; name: string; }
#

For renamed re-exports (export {foo as bar}), points to the original declaration. This declaration's name is the alias; aliasOf.name is the original name.

For renames out of the default slot (export {default as bar} from './x' where ./x is export default ...), aliasOf.name is 'default' — the canonical's actual symbol name. Consumers locate the canonical by (aliasOf.module, aliasOf.name).

Svelte component exception: when the source is a .svelte file (e.g., export {default as Foo} from './X.svelte'), the canonical's name is the component name (derived from the filename), so aliasOf.name is the component name ('X'), NOT 'default'. Consumers that branch on aliasOf.name === 'default' to detect default-rename should additionally check whether aliasOf.module ends with .svelte.

Different from alsoExportedFrom: aliases create new API surface names, while alsoExportedFrom tracks additional import paths for the same name.

A type-only rename of a value (export type {someConst as c} from './x') synthesizes a normal alias — declarations carry no type-only marker.

deprecatedMessage
?: string
#

Deprecation message from @deprecated tag.

since
?: string
#

Version introduced, from @since tag.

internalMessage
?: string
#

Internal-API marker from the @internal tag. Presence means the tag was written; an empty string is a bare tag with no trailing prose.

A marker, not an exclusion: @internal means "not stable public API" (TSDoc semantics) while the declaration, member, or prop stays documented — unlike @nodocs, which removes a declaration from output entirely (and is ignored on props and members).

mutates
?: Record<string, string>
#

Mutation documentation from @mutates tags (non-standard), mapping keys to descriptions.

Keys are intentionally unvalidated — typically a parameter name, but authors may also use compound paths (this.foo, obj.field) or multi-word external state references. Backticks are stripped from keys so `` a `` and a normalize to one key; an empty-string value is a bare tag with no description. The schema accepts any string key so consumers can render whatever the author wrote.

On a component prop it declares the component's mutation contract for the value it's handed: the component writes into the prop's object or array in place (@mutates items - appends the selected entry, @mutates options.cache - fills on first render). Reassigning a prop is not a mutation in this sense (bindable covers it), though a $bindable prop can carry both.

docComment
?: string
#

JSDoc/TSDoc comment.

typeSignature
?: string
#

Full TypeScript type signature.

sourceLine
?: number
#

1-based line in the source file, a positive integer. Synthesized aliases (see aliasOf) carry the local export specifier's line, not the canonical's.

ParameterJson
#

types.ts view source

value + type

also exported from index.ts

Parameter information for functions and methods.

Kept distinct from ComponentPropJson despite structural similarity. Function parameters form a tuple with positional semantics: calling order matters (fn(a, b) vs fn(b, a)), may include rest parameters and destructuring patterns.

Carries no doc fields beyond description, unlike ComponentPropJson: a parameter's docs come from one @param line, while a prop has a JSDoc block of its own.

import {ParameterJson} from 'svelte-docinfo/types.ts';

inheritance

extends: SchemaStrictObjectOutput<typeof ParameterJsonEntries>

members

name
: string
#

Parameter name (e.g., options, args); rest-ness is carried by rest, never the name.

type
: string
#

Resolved TypeScript type string (e.g., string, Record<string, unknown>).

optional
: boolean
#

Whether a caller may omit the argument, by the checker's isOptionalParameter: a ? token, an initializer with no required parameter after it (b = 0), and in JS a bracketed @param {T} [b] or @param {T=} b. When set, type and typeInfo drop a top-level undefined (the optional widening, or one an initialized parameter's type already holds), so optional carries it alone. A rest parameter is never optional.

rest
: boolean
#

Whether the parameter uses rest syntax (...args).

pattern
?: string
#

A destructured parameter's binding pattern ({ a, b = 1 }, [a, b]), printed on one line with its defaults kept and comments dropped (a string default that spans lines keeps its line breaks). Such a parameter has no name of its own, so name is the one TypeScript gives it by position (__0 for the first parameter, __1 for the second, a this parameter counted); a renderer shows the pattern in its place. Absent on an identifier-named parameter.

docName
?: string
#

The name a destructured parameter's @param tag gives it (options for fn({a, b}: T) under @param options), the tag TypeScript matches by position; on a callable property's function type (m: ({a}: O) => void), the property's tag in that position. A renderer can anchor or link the parameter by it where name is only the positional __0. Absent on an identifier-named parameter, with no such tag, and for an array pattern's tag (@param [a, b]), whose name is no name.

typeInfo
?: TypeJson
#

Structured type; absent when type is the whole story (see TypeJson).

description
?: string
#

Description from @param tag.

defaultValue
?: string
#

The initializer's source text, verbatim (e.g., "'hello'", 42, () => 10) — quotes included, no normalization; consumers render it as highlighted TS. Without an initializer, the default a bracketed @param {T} [b=0] writes, verbatim the same way.

propertyDescriptions
?: Record<string, string>
#

Descriptions for properties of a named object parameter, from dotted @param tags (@param obj.prop - ...), the ones TypeScript nests under a braced @param {object} obj included.

Keyed by the sub-path relative to this parameter — @param obj.prop becomes {prop: '...'}, @param obj.a.b becomes {'a.b': '...'}, and an array element's @param arr[].prop becomes {'[].prop': '...'}. Keys are unvalidated against the parameter's actual type (matching the @mutates philosophy); absent when no dotted @param tags reference this parameter. Only populated for function/method/constructor signature parameters.

Matching is by the parameter's name. A destructured parameter (fn({a, b}: T)), which TypeScript names __0, takes the @param tag in its position as TypeScript does (@param options then @param options.a), where that tag isn't itself dotted; its description comes from the same tag.

parseModuleJson
#

types.ts view source

also exported from index.ts

parseModuleJson(value: unknown): ModuleJson

Validate a ModuleJson, restoring the defaults the wire form omits.

The stable way to validate a module or restore what compactReplacer stripped (empty arrays, false booleans), independent of the schema library behind ModuleJson.

The result is not a fresh copy: an object that needed no default is the one in value, so the result can be value itself or share objects with it, and mutating one then mutates the other.

import {parseModuleJson} from 'svelte-docinfo/types.ts';

parameters

value
: unknown
#

a module, typically from JSON.parse of compact output

returns

the validated module with every default present

throws

  • Error - when value doesn't match the schema; the message lists the reported issues, one per line, as path: message (declarations.1.kind: expected …, received "funtion"), the value that failed in place of its type when it's a string, number, or boolean (an unknown key's never), the dot path omitted for an issue at the root, and ends with a line saying there may be more when it holds a hundred. The class is the schema library's (fuz_schema's SchemaError, the structured list on issues), so catch it as a plain Error unless you depend on fuz_schema
  • RangeError - when value nests deeper than the call stack allows, as a TypeJson tree thousands of levels deep does

"$state" | "$state.raw" | "$derived" | "$derived.by"

type "$state" | "$state.raw" | "$derived" | "$derived.by"

Reactivity flavor for a variable declaration or class field, captured from the rune call at the initializer (e.g., let count = $state(0)).

Only the value-producing reactivity runes are represented here — $props and $bindable are modeled separately as ComponentPropJson.bindable (and prop-presence on the props array), which a legacy export let prop sets too. A renderer wanting "all rune annotations across declarations and props" needs to read both this field and ComponentPropJson.bindable.

  • $state — deeply reactive proxy
  • $state.raw — reference-only reactive (no proxy)
  • $derived — recomputed from dependencies (re-assignable)
  • $derived.by — same as $derived, with a function argument

Detection is syntactic (AST-based) and runs on every analyzed file regardless of extension. Most reactive declarations live in .svelte, .svelte.ts, or .svelte.js, but the field will also surface on any .ts/.js file that uses the same rune call patterns — by design, so documentation pipelines can capture any rune-shaped declaration their conventions choose to expose.

ReExportJson
#

types.ts view source

value + type

also exported from index.ts

A same-name re-export edge, from the re-exporting module's side.

Each entry on ModuleJson.reExports records that the module's source contains export {name} from ..., or the import-then-export form it stands for (import {name} from ...; export {name}, export default X over a default import), where the canonical declaration lives in module. This is the forward view of the same fact that alsoExportedFrom records on the canonical declaration — consumers resolve the canonical by (module, name), the same lookup contract as aliasOf.

Same-name re-exports of analyzed source only. Renamed re-exports appear as declarations with aliasOf in the re-exporting module; star exports live in ModuleJson.starExports; external re-exports in ModuleJson.externalReExports / externalStarExports. Use resolveExportSurface (in postprocess.ts) to combine all of these into a module's full export surface — it handles the name dedup (a documented same-name re-export appears both here and as a synthesized alias declaration) and the ES star semantics (explicit exports shadow star-projected ones, names ambiguous between stars are excluded, default doesn't project).

module points at the *canonical* module (multi-hop chains are resolved), not the immediate specifier in the export statement. For Svelte default-slot re-exports (export {default} from './X.svelte', or `import X from './X.svelte'; export default X), name` is the component name derived from the filename ('X'), matching the canonical declaration's name — the same exception documented on aliasOf. Because of that re-keying, two entries in one module can share a name (a re-keyed component colliding with a same-name re-export from another module); (module, name) pairs remain unique (exact duplicates are deduped at construction).

@nodocs on the export statement suppresses the entry (and the alsoExportedFrom back-link). When the canonical declaration itself is @nodocs, the entry still exists but has no matching back-link. module is always a module in the same result: a re-export whose canonical module emits nothing (gated, or outside the analyzed inputs) is a declaration with aliasOf in the re-exporting module instead, and aliasOf.module is the one field that can name a module the result doesn't contain.

A star over a module that emits nothing produces entries here too, one per projected binding whose canonical does emit, with the star statement's line and type-only-ness (see ModuleJson.starExports).

The exported name. Always populated. The default-export slot is named 'default', except a Svelte component, which takes its filename-derived name ('X' for X.svelte) — 'default' is the symbol's actual name in JS (import {default as X} and ns.default both expose it directly), and import X from 'mod' is sugar for import {default as X}. aliasOf
?: { module: string; name: string; }
#

For renamed re-exports (export {foo as bar}), points to the original declaration. This declaration's name is the alias; aliasOf.name is the original name.

For renames out of the default slot (export {default as bar} from './x' where ./x is export default ...), aliasOf.name is 'default' — the canonical's actual symbol name. Consumers locate the canonical by (aliasOf.module, aliasOf.name).

Svelte component exception: when the source is a .svelte file (e.g., export {default as Foo} from './X.svelte'), the canonical's name is the component name (derived from the filename), so aliasOf.name is the component name ('X'), NOT 'default'. Consumers that branch on aliasOf.name === 'default' to detect default-rename should additionally check whether aliasOf.module ends with .svelte.

Different from alsoExportedFrom: aliases create new API surface names, while alsoExportedFrom tracks additional import paths for the same name.

A type-only rename of a value (export type {someConst as c} from './x') synthesizes a normal alias — declarations carry no type-only marker.

A marker, not an exclusion: @internal means "not stable public API" (TSDoc semantics) while the declaration, member, or prop stays documented — unlike @nodocs, which removes a declaration from output entirely (and is ignored on props and members).

Mutation documentation from @mutates tags (non-standard), mapping keys to descriptions.

Keys are intentionally unvalidated — typically a parameter name, but authors may also use compound paths (this.foo, obj.field) or multi-word external state references. Backticks are stripped from keys so `` a `` and a normalize to one key; an empty-string value is a bare tag with no description. The schema accepts any string key so consumers can render whatever the author wrote.

On a component prop it declares the component's mutation contract for the value it's handed: the component writes into the prop's object or array in place (@mutates items - appends the selected entry, @mutates options.cache - fills on first render). Reassigning a prop is not a mutation in this sense (bindable covers it), though a $bindable prop can carry both.

?: string

JSDoc/TSDoc comment.

typeSignature
?: string
#

Full TypeScript type signature.

sourceLine
?: number

import {TypeDeclarationJson} from 'svelte-docinfo/types.ts';

inheritance

extends: SchemaStrictObjectOutput<typeof TypeDeclarationJsonEntries>

members

kind
: "type"
#
externalTypes
: string[]
#

External types whose contributions are filtered out of members.

Filtering is by declaration origin at every granularity — named properties, index signatures, call/construct signatures — so a purely structural external branch (an index-signature-only or callable-only interface) is recorded here exactly like a named-property bag. A declaration-less contribution (the index signature the checker synthesizes for a mapped-type instantiation like Record<string, X> or Partial<Indexed>) is kept in members and records nothing here.

Covers every composition the written type reaches: an intersection or union branch, a bare or indexed-access reference, and a type composed behind a project-local name (type Base = Bag & {…}, a local interface's extends, a local container's accessed property LocalMap['a']). Entries carry the written form with two normalizations: an identifier bound by an import rename at the definition site (import type {Bag as B}) resolves back to the name its module exports, and a type parameter bound inside the descent substitutes its written argument (interface A<T> extends ExtG<T> reached via extends A<string> records ExtG<string>). Each distinct contributor appears once, in source order; a generic reference keeps its arguments. A local name is used only when it hides a definition the walk cannot traverse — a mapped or conditional type.

Names carry no module, so the dedupe is by name alone: two *distinct* external types sharing an exported name (one from each of two packages) collapse to a single entry.

see also

  • ComponentDeclarationJson.externalTypes, InterfaceDeclarationJson.externalTypes, ClassDeclarationJson.externalTypes for the same field on the other kinds, and ClassDeclarationJson.extends, ClassDeclarationJson.implements, InterfaceDeclarationJson.extends for the verbatim own-clause heritage fields. Field shapes mirror TS syntax.

members
: (FunctionMemberJson | VariableMemberJson | ConstructorMemberJson)[]
#

Type members: properties (property and method signatures) first, then index signatures (string, number), then call and construct signatures.

Tells consumers the name is importable as a runtime value: import {Foo}, never import type {Foo} (see generateImport).

Type aliases print as their own name for every non-interned type, so the tree is emitted there whatever its shape — the exception is object and function roots, whose content members already carries.

members
?: (FunctionMemberJsonInput | VariableMemberJsonInput | ConstructorMemberJsonInput)[]
#

Type members: properties (property and method signatures) first, then index signatures (string, number), then call and construct signatures.

mergedValue
?: boolean
#

The exported name also carries a value meaning — a merged value+type symbol (const Foo = z.strictObject({...}) + `type Foo = z.infer<typeof Foo>`, the schema/type pattern), where the type alias wins the declaration slot and the value's own type goes undocumented. Tells consumers the name is importable as a runtime value: import {Foo}, never import type {Foo} (see generateImport).

see also

  • InterfaceDeclarationJson.mergedValue

alsoExportedFrom
?: string[]
#

Module paths (relative to sourceRoot) that re-export this declaration under the same name. The canonical declaration lives in this module's declarations array; these paths are additional import locations for the same thing.

The same edges appear from the re-exporting side as ModuleJson.reExports — use that when asking "what does this module re-export" instead of inverting these arrays. The two can disagree at the margins: a reExports entry whose canonical declaration is @nodocs (or whose module isn't in the analyzed set) has no back-link here.

Consumer note: To build a complete re-export map, scan two fields:

  1. alsoExportedFrom on each declaration — same-name re-exports
  2. aliasOf on declarations — renamed re-exports (separate declarations)
aliasOf
?: { module: string; name: string; }
#

For renamed re-exports (export {foo as bar}), points to the original declaration. This declaration's name is the alias; aliasOf.name is the original name.

For renames out of the default slot (export {default as bar} from './x' where ./x is export default ...), aliasOf.name is 'default' — the canonical's actual symbol name. Consumers locate the canonical by (aliasOf.module, aliasOf.name).

Svelte component exception: when the source is a .svelte file (e.g., export {default as Foo} from './X.svelte'), the canonical's name is the component name (derived from the filename), so aliasOf.name is the component name ('X'), NOT 'default'. Consumers that branch on aliasOf.name === 'default' to detect default-rename should additionally check whether aliasOf.module ends with .svelte.

Different from alsoExportedFrom: aliases create new API surface names, while alsoExportedFrom tracks additional import paths for the same name.

A type-only rename of a value (export type {someConst as c} from './x') synthesizes a normal alias — declarations carry no type-only marker.

partial
?: boolean
#

Whether extraction failed partway through, leaving some fields missing (e.g., typeSignature, parameters).

examples

throws

since

internalMessage

Internal-API marker from the @internal tag. Presence means the tag was written; an empty string is a bare tag with no trailing prose.

A marker, not an exclusion: @internal means "not stable public API" (TSDoc semantics) while the declaration, member, or prop stays documented — unlike @nodocs, which removes a declaration from output entirely (and is ignored on props and members).

Backticks are stripped from keys so `` a `` and a normalize to one key; an empty-string value is a bare tag with no description. The schema accepts any string key so consumers can render whatever the author wrote.

On a component prop it declares the component's mutation contract for the value it's handed: the component writes into the prop's object or array in place (@mutates items - appends the selected entry, @mutates options.cache - fills on first render). Reassigning a prop is not a mutation in this sense (bindable covers it), though a $bindable prop can carry both.
